blocks.value: Java provides classes for reading and writing both raw bytes and text. The ones you'll use most: FileInputStream and FileOutputStream read and write raw file data; BufferedReader and BufferedWriter read and write text more efficiently by buffering characters instead of handling them one at a time.

To open a file for writing, Files.newOutputStream() takes a Path and a StandardOpenOption. The options you'll reach for most: CREATE (open the file if it exists, or create it if it doesn't), WRITE (open for writing), and APPEND (add new data to the end instead of overwriting).

To open a file for reading, Files.newInputStream() takes a Path and returns a stream of bytes. Wrapping that in a BufferedReader lets you call readLine() to read a full line of text at a time instead of one character at a time.
Common BufferedReader methods: readLine() (read a line of text), read() (read a single character), close() (release the stream's resources).
Common BufferedWriter methods: write(...) (write text), newLine() (write a line separator), flush() (force buffered data out), close() (flush and release resources).
